research: Commit dff50350e split the bounded subprocess pump out of wre_git_bounded_io.py and removed _terminate_reader.

The new test exercises run_bounded_process and records kill, 30-second reap, both pipe closes, and 5-second reader join.

macro_pass: The archive plus adjacent WRE differential-plan runtime suites passed 54 tests in 26.45 seconds.
No production src file, registry entry, runtime route, environment, Holo owner, extension artifact, or sites/ path changed.

hard_think: Restoring the private helper would hide the refactor drift while adding a dead compatibility seam.
Directly testing _terminate_threads would repeat the same private coupling and remain vulnerable to another internal split.
The public behavior is the stable contract and can be falsified without launching a real child process.
dialectic_sweep: Deleting the stale test was rejected because process cleanup remains load-bearing.
Bundling the correction into Phase 2C was rejected because it would contaminate attribution of the new artifact slice.
A focused public-interface test is smaller and more durable than restoring or patching private helpers.
first_principles: Tests should bind observable public behavior, not implementation-private names.
A timeout process pump must terminate the child, close all owned pipes, join workers, and preserve the timeout signal.
The smallest valid repair is one test evolution plus truthful operational memory and no production code.

nonclaims: No production bounded-process behavior or public Python API changed.
No child process was launched by the corrected timeout unit test.
No RedDog packaging artifact, runtime activation, Holo route, A-grade, or RSI claim is made.
